steps.tx: **Direct allorecognition** occurs when recipient T cell receptors directly bind intact donor **MHC** molecules on donor passenger dendritic cells, driving vigorous acute **cellular rejection**. In contrast, **indirect allorecognition** involves recipient antigen-presenting cells processing donor peptides, mediating chronic antibody-mediated rejection. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: The **Complement-dependent cytotoxicity** crossmatch, or **CDC crossmatch**, detects cytotoxic anti-donor **HLA** antibodies. A positive T-cell CDC crossmatch represents an absolute contraindication to transplantation due to inevitable **hyperacute rejection** and immediate graft loss. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

left.title: Positive T-Cell CDC Crossmatch
points: Antibody target: High-titer complement-fixing anti-HLA class I
Clinical consequence: Inevitable hyperacute graft thrombosis
Transplant decision: Absolute contraindication to surgery
Alternative: Enter paired kidney exchange or desensitization

right.title: Isolated B-Cell CDC Crossmatch
points: Antibody target: Anti-HLA class II or low-titer autoantibodies
Clinical consequence: Increased risk of acute rejection
Transplant decision: Proceed with caution under augmented induction
Alternative: Verify specificity via Luminex single-antigen beads

steps.tx: The **Flow cytometric crossmatch**, or **FCXM**, is **10**- to **100**-fold more sensitive than CDC for identifying low-titer non-complement-fixing **anti-HLA antibodies**, reliably predicting early allograft dysfunction and subclinical acute cellular or antibody-mediated rejection. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: **Luminex** **single-antigen bead** assays characterize circulating **donor-specific antibodies**, abbreviated as DSA, and quantify mean fluorescence intensity, or **MFI**, where thresholds of **1000** to **5000** define clinically significant immunological risk. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: **Calculated Panel Reactive Antibody**, or **cPRA**, quantifies the percentage of deceased donors in a donor pool who express HLA antigens against which a candidate possesses **unacceptable antigens**, reflecting the statistical difficulty of securing a compatible crossmatch-negative graft. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: T cell activation mandates three signals: **Signal 1** via TCR-MHC binding; **Signal 2** costimulation blocked by **belatacept**; and **Signal 3** driven by IL-2 receptor signaling activating **mTOR**, targeted by basiliximab and mTOR inhibitors. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: **ABO-incompatible** kidney transplantation requires rigorous pre-transplant **desensitization** utilizing B-cell depletion with **rituximab**, plasmapheresis or immunoadsorption, and IVIg, targeting anti-A/B **isoagglutinin** titers of **1**:**8** to **1**:**16** at surgery. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients. Structured clinical management and regular follow-up help guide therapeutic optimization and prevent disease complications.

steps.tx: **Imlifidase**, known as **IdeS**, is a recombinant **IgG-degrading** enzyme derived from Streptococcus pyogenes that cleaves all human IgG into F(ab')2 and Fc fragments within **2** to **6** hours, enabling successful desensitization and transplantation in sensitized **cPRA** **100%** candidates. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.
